row.evidence: Overleaf's Group SSO FAQ: "Because your system will not be provisioning users in Overleaf, SCIM isn’t supported or required."
row.notes: Unchanged from June (none). Plans renamed: the June 'Group Standard'/'Group Professional' are now Standard ($199/user/yr) and Pro ($399/user/yr), bought per user with 10% off group licenses; Organizations (20+ users) is Contact Sales. SAML Group SSO and Managed Users require a Pro group. Users self-provision via email invitations (JIT link to SSO); domain capture (limited beta) auto-enrols users. Deleting a user in the IdP does not touch the Overleaf account. Audit logs (Standard+) are UI/CSV only. No admin API.

plans.name: Standard
plans.notes: Comparison table marks Audit logging as included (UI/CSV, not an API).

plans.name: Pro
plans.notes: Group SSO and Managed Users need a Pro group subscription.

limitations.text: Deleting a user in the IdP does not delete or remove their Overleaf account; removal is manual in the group admin UI.

scim.notes: Overleaf's Group SSO FAQ states SCIM is not supported because users provision their own accounts.

audit_log_api.notes: Group subscription audit logs are available in the admin UI and as CSV export, not via a documented API.

user_api.notes: No public admin or user-management API is documented in docs.overleaf.com (llms.txt index); group management is via the subscription admin UI.

okta.notes: okta.com/integrations/overleaf/ returns 404; Overleaf documents generic SAML 2.0 setup with Okta.

entra.notes: learn.microsoft.com overleaf-tutorial returns 404; Overleaf documents generic SAML 2.0 setup with Entra.

fallbacks.other_sync: Domain capture (limited beta for selected Pro groups) auto-enrols users under verified domains as managed users

citations.title: Group SSO FAQs
citations.quote: Because your system will not be provisioning users in Overleaf, SCIM isn’t supported or required.

citations.title: Group SSO FAQs
citations.quote: Yes. Overleaf accounts are provisioned by users who receive email invitations to join their account to the group and link to their SSO identity.

citations.title: Group SSO FAQs
citations.quote: No. Deleting a user in your IdP will not delete their account in Overleaf. Overleaf accounts are deleted in Overleaf by the account owner.

citations.title: Setting up Group SSO
citations.quote: **Group SSO is available to Overleaf Pro group subscribers only**

citations.title: Setting up Group SSO
citations.quote: Our group SSO uses SAML 2.0, allowing it to integrate with a wide variety of Identity Providers (IdPs), including Microsoft Entra/Azure, Okta, Shibboleth, Jumpcloud, and many others.

citations.title: Adding and removing users and managers
citations.quote: Removing a user from a group subscription will place the user's account back on the Free plan.

citations.title: Managed Users

citations.title: Managed Users
citations.quote: **Delete User (Destructive):** This action deletes the user account and transfers ownership of the projects within that account to another designated managed user in the group.

citations.title: Domain management
citations.quote: Domain management features, including domain verification and domain capture, are currently available to selected Pro group subscriptions through a **limited beta program**.

citations.title: Domain management
citations.quote: These features are sometimes referred to as **domain claiming**, and enable Just-In-Time (JIT) SSO provisioning, account consolidation, and mandatory SSO routing.
